sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was reduced: Q1'22 paid net adds forecast of 2.5m is well below the 4.0m in the year-ago quarter, and full-year 2022 operating margin guidance of 19%-20% is below the 21% achieved in 2021. Management explicitly attributes the margin headwind to a stronger US dollar, which is a structural FX risk given ~60% of revenue is outside the US and they do not hedge. Additionally, management notes that acquisition growth has not yet re-accelerated to pre-Covid levels, citing ongoing Covid overhang and macro-economic hardship in several parts of the world like LATAM. These factors collectively indicate a lowered forward outlook.

summary.revenue: Q4'21 revenue of $7,709 million grew 16% year over year. Full year 2021 revenue of $29,698 million grew 19% year over year.
summary.eps: Q4'21 diluted EPS of $1.33 vs. $1.19 a year ago, including a $104m non-cash unrealized gain from FX remeasurement on Euro denominated debt.
summary.guidance: Q1'22 forecast: revenue $7,903 million, operating margin 22.3%, diluted EPS $2.86, paid net adds 2.5m. Full year 2022: targeting operating margin of 19%-20% (assuming no material swings in foreign currency from current levels).
summary.margin: Q4'21 operating margin of 8% vs. 14.4% in Q4'20. Full year 2021 operating margin of 21% vs. 18% in 2020. Q1'22 forecast operating margin of 22.3%.
key_risks: Stronger US dollar: with ~60% of revenue outside the US, the dollar's appreciation over the past six months is estimated to cost roughly $1 billion in expected 2022 revenue, translating into an estimated two percentage point negative impact on 2022 operating margin.
Acquisition growth has not yet re-accelerated to pre-Covid levels, possibly due to ongoing Covid overhang and macro-economic hardship in several parts of the world like LATAM.
Increased competition from streaming alternatives may be affecting marginal growth.
Quarterly guidance volatility: as membership base grows, there will naturally be more volatility in absolute paid net adds performance vs. forecast.
key_opportunities: Streaming supplants linear entertainment around the world, providing long-term growth prospects.
Under 10% of total TV screen time in the US, Netflix's biggest market, indicates tremendous room for growth if service continues to improve.
Expansion of mobile games portfolio across casual and core gaming genres to learn what members enjoy most.
Price reductions in India to make Netflix more accessible and strengthen value perception.
Anticipated positive free cash flow for full year 2022 and beyond, enabling shareholder returns via stock repurchases.
